name: HivePunk 547
subject: LangMem
thesis: LangMem is a useful LangGraph-native memory layer with demonstrated adoption, but its pre-1.0 release cadence and LLM-dependent dedup and retrieval quality make it a proceed-with-tests choice rather than a proven default.

claims.label: FACT

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: LangMem helps agents learn and adapt from interactions by extracting important information, optimizing behavior through prompt refinement, and maintaining long-term memory.
claims.quote: LangMem helps agents learn and adapt from their interactions over time. It provides tooling to extract important information from conversations, optimize agent behavior through prompt refinement, and maintain long-term memory.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: LangMem is installed with pip install -U langmem.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: LangMem has three memory types: semantic, episodic and procedural.
claims.quote: Three memory types — semantic (facts/knowledge), episodic (past experiences), and procedural (learned behaviors/prompt rules) — modeled after human memory

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: LangMem has two integration modes: hot-path tools and background memory managers.
claims.quote: Two integration modes: hot-path tools agents call during conversations, and background memory managers that extract memories asynchronously

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: LangMem had about 746K monthly PyPI downloads and 5M+ total as of June 2026.
claims.quote: Real adoption (~746K monthly PyPI downloads, 5M+ total as of June 2026) but still pre-1.0 — latest release is 0.0.30 from October 2025, with active repo commits continuing into June 2026

claims.label: FACT

claims.quote: It ships as a lightweight pip install langmem package with ~1.5K GitHub stars as of June 2026 [ 1 ] .

claims.quote: All persistence, indexing, and search are delegated to langgraph.store.BaseStore ( InMemoryStore for dev, AsyncPostgresStore for prod).

claims.quote: Zero dedup, zero enrichment, zero quality/salience gating — the LLM decides everything via the tool's instruction string.

risks: Pre-1.0 status and slow release cadence: latest PyPI release 0.0.30 from October 2025 despite ongoing repo activity.
Hot-path memory tool has zero dedup, zero enrichment and zero quality/salience gating, with the LLM deciding via the tool instruction string, per the somnigraph source analysis.
Retrieval is pure semantic vector search delegated to BaseStore, with no BM25/FTS, reranker or graph expansion described in that source.
No custom storage, themes, priority, decay, validity intervals, source attribution or trust in the base memory schema described in that source.
Framework choice risk: positioned for memory primitives inside LangGraph, rather than memory as a service behind any framework.
unknowns: Whether AlexisOlson/somnigraph is still shipping: None of its commits in the last 30 days is real work.
The latest PyPI release of LangMem is 0.0.30, published October 27, 2025.: Its source does not state 30.
LangMem combines high download traction with pre-1.0 status, so adoption does not by itself prove release maturity.: It was worked out from something that is not a verified fact.
Whether LangMem will reach a 1.0 release or maintain a faster release cadence.: A public roadmap, release plan, or newer PyPI release after 0.0.30 from October 27, 2025.
wouldChangeMind: A newer PyPI release at or above 1.0, or a public roadmap committing to one.
Independent benchmark results showing LangMem beat no-tool and alternative baselines on cost and quality for long histories.
A security audit or documented production case studies covering memory corruption, privacy, and multi-user isolation.
